import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.64

by A. K. Rumyantsev, D. M. Smirnov

Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

A quasiidentity in the language of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \; \bigl((u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v\bigr),$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_1, \dots, x_n$ (for $k = 0$ this
is an identity). A set $\Sigma$ of quasiidentities is a *basis of quasiidentities* of a class
$\mathscr{K}$ of groups if a group satisfies $\Sigma$ exactly when it satisfies every
quasiidentity that holds in all members of $\mathscr{K}$, i.e. $\Sigma$ axiomatizes (modulo the
group axioms) the quasivariety generated by $\mathscr{K}$. The basis $\Sigma$ is *independent* if
no member of $\Sigma$ is a consequence (modulo the group axioms) of the remaining members.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«8.64»

blocks.code:
structure Quasiidentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_i = v_i$, as pairs of words $(u_i, v_i)$. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as the pair of words $(u, v)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
blocks.docstring:
A quasiidentity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$(u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v,$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. Whether a group
satisfies such a formula depends only on the classes of these words modulo the group axioms, so
the words are represented as elements of the free group on `Fin n`. The case $k = 0$ (no premises)
gives the identities.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib.ModelTheory (FirstOrder.Language.Sentence, BoundedFormula) — but Mathlib only provides `Language.ring`, no group language, and building one plus universal-Horn syntax would be far heavier than the free-group representation, which is the standard way quasiidentities of groups are written.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity
justification.why_needed: A quasiidentity (universal Horn sentence) in the language of groups: number of variables n, a list of premise word-pairs and a conclusion word-pair, with words as elements of FreeGroup (Fin n). Mathlib has no group language / quasiidentity notion.

blocks.name: Quasiidentity
blocks.text:
/--
A quasiidentity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$(u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v,$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. Whether a group
satisfies such a formula depends only on the classes of these words modulo the group axioms, so
the words are represented as elements of the free group on `Fin n`. The case $k = 0$ (no premises)
gives the identities.
-/
structure Quasiidentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_i = v_i$, as pairs of words $(u_i, v_i)$. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as the pair of words $(u, v)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
namespace Quasiidentity

blocks.code:
def Holds (q : Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` satisfies the quasiidentity `q` if for every assignment `x` of the variables in `G`
under which all the premises of `q` hold, the conclusion of `q` holds. Words are evaluated at `x`
by the homomorphism `FreeGroup.lift x`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Structure.realize / `⊨` — not applicable without a group language.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity.Holds
justification.why_needed: Satisfaction of a quasiidentity by a group: for every assignment of variables, if all premises evaluate equal (via FreeGroup.lift) so does the conclusion.

blocks.name: Holds
blocks.text:
/--
A group `G` satisfies the quasiidentity `q` if for every assignment `x` of the variables in `G`
under which all the premises of `q` hold, the conclusion of `q` holds. Words are evaluated at `x`
by the homomorphism `FreeGroup.lift x`.
-/
def Holds (q : Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

blocks.code:
def SetHolds (S : Set Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, q.Holds G
blocks.docstring: A group `G` satisfies a set `S` of quasiidentities if it satisfies every member of `S`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity.SetHolds
justification.why_needed: A group satisfies every member of a set of quasiidentities.

blocks.name: SetHolds

blocks.code:
def Follows (S : Set Quasiidentity) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G → q.Holds G
blocks.docstring:
The quasiidentity `q` is a consequence of the set `S` of quasiidentities (modulo the group
axioms): every group satisfying `S` satisfies `q`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity.Follows
justification.why_needed: Semantic consequence modulo the group axioms: every group (in Type) satisfying S satisfies q.

blocks.name: Follows
blocks.text:
/--
The quasiidentity `q` is a consequence of the set `S` of quasiidentities (modulo the group
axioms): every group satisfying `S` satisfies `q`.
-/
def Follows (S : Set Quasiidentity) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G → q.Holds G

blocks.code:
def Independent (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Follows (S \ {q}) q
blocks.docstring:
A set `S` of quasiidentities is independent if no member of `S` is a consequence of the
remaining members of `S`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity.Independent
justification.why_needed: No member of S follows from S \ {q}.

blocks.name: Independent
blocks.text:
/--
A set `S` of quasiidentities is independent if no member of `S` is a consequence of the
remaining members of `S`.
-/
def Independent (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Follows (S \ {q}) q

blocks.code:
def HoldsInClass (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G → q.Holds G
blocks.docstring: The quasiidentity `q` holds in the class `𝒦` of groups if every group in `𝒦` satisfies `q`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity.HoldsInClass
justification.why_needed: q holds in every group of a class 𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop.

blocks.name: HoldsInClass
blocks.text:
/--
The quasiidentity `q` holds in the class `𝒦` of groups if every group in `𝒦` satisfies `q`.
-/
def HoldsInClass (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G → q.Holds G

blocks.code:
def IsBasis (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G ↔ ∀ q, HoldsInClass 𝒦 q → q.Holds G
blocks.docstring:
A set `S` of quasiidentities is a basis of quasiidentities of the class `𝒦` of groups if a group
satisfies `S` exactly when it satisfies every quasiidentity that holds in the class `𝒦`.
Equivalently, `S` consists of quasiidentities holding in `𝒦` and every quasiidentity holding in
`𝒦` is a consequence of `S`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity.IsBasis
justification.why_needed: S is a basis of quasiidentities of the class 𝒦: a group satisfies S iff it satisfies every quasiidentity holding in 𝒦.

blocks.name: IsBasis
blocks.text:
/--
A set `S` of quasiidentities is a basis of quasiidentities of the class `𝒦` of groups if a group
satisfies `S` exactly when it satisfies every quasiidentity that holds in the class `𝒦`.
Equivalently, `S` consists of quasiidentities holding in `𝒦` and every quasiidentity holding in
`𝒦` is a consequence of `S`.
-/
def IsBasis (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G ↔ ∀ q, HoldsInClass 𝒦 q → q.Holds G

blocks.code:
def commLaw : Quasiidentity where
  numVars := 2
  premises := []
  conclusion := (.of 0 * .of 1, .of 1 * .of 0)
blocks.docstring: The commutative law $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$, an identity (a quasiidentity with no premises).

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.64».Quasiidentity.commLaw
justification.why_needed: Test-only example (commutative law as an identity) used to unit-test `Holds` on a CommGroup and on Equiv.Perm (Fin 3).

blocks.text:
/-- The commutative law $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$, an identity (a quasiidentity with no premises). -/
def commLaw : Quasiidentity where
  numVars := 2
  premises := []
  conclusion := (.of 0 * .of 1, .of 1 * .of 0)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem commLaw_holds (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : commLaw.Holds G := by
  intro x _
  simp [commLaw, mul_comm]
blocks.name: commLaw_holds
blocks.text:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem commLaw_holds (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : commLaw.Holds G := by
  intro x _
  simp [commLaw, mul_comm]

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_commLaw_holds_equiv_perm_fin_three : ¬ commLaw.Holds (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) := by
  intro h
  have := h ![Equiv.swap 0 1, Equiv.swap 1 2] (by simp [commLaw])
  simp [commLaw] at this
  exact absurd (congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe this) 0) (by decide)

theorem IsBasis.holdsInClass {𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop} {S : Set Quasiidentity}

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question: it asks whether there exists a set Σ of quasiidentities (universal Horn sentences in the language of groups) that is a basis for the quasiidentities of the class of finite groups — i.e. a group satisfies all quasiidentities true in every finite group iff it satisfies Σ (Σ axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by the finite groups, in the presence of the group axioms) — with Σ independent (no member of Σ follows from the remaining ones modulo the group axioms); the answer is a Prop via answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ Σ, ... in the repo's style.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state semantically the same thing and all compile: a quasiidentity is finitely many premise equations plus one conclusion between group words (elements of a free group, i.e. terms modulo the group axioms); Σ is a basis iff, for every group G, G ⊨ Σ ↔ G ⊨ every quasiidentity true in all finite groups (so Mod(Σ) = Q(finite groups) among groups, which also forces Σ ⊆ Q(Fin)); Σ is independent iff for each q ∈ Σ some group satisfies Σ \ {q} but not q. This matches the standard (Mal'cev/Gorbunov/Budkin) meaning of 'independent basis of quasiidentities of a class of groups', taken modulo the group axioms as the decomposition note requires. Checked: answer(sorry) scopes the whole existential; iff direction of the basis condition; independence equals irredundancy for a basis; restricting groups to `Type` is lossless because quasiidentities are universal sentences (any countermodel shrinks to a countable subgroup); List/Finset premises, Fin n/ℕ variables and free-group representatives do not affect existence of an independent basis (an independent set cannot contain two equivalent members). c01 was chosen because it is the best documented, parametrizes `IsBasis`/`HoldsInClass` by a class of groups, and includes the API/test lemmas that CONTRIBUTING.md asks for with bespoke definitions. Only edit: added AMS 8 (general algebraic systems / quasivarieties) to the main theorem's tags.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.64

by A. K. Rumyantsev, D. M. Smirnov

Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

A quasiidentity in the language of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \; \bigl((u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v\bigr),$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_1, \dots, x_n$ (for $k = 0$ this
is an identity). A set $\Sigma$ of quasiidentities is a *basis of quasiidentities* of a class
$\mathscr{K}$ of groups if a group satisfies $\Sigma$ exactly when it satisfies every
quasiidentity that holds in all members of $\mathscr{K}$, i.e. $\Sigma$ axiomatizes (modulo the
group axioms) the quasivariety generated by $\mathscr{K}$. The basis $\Sigma$ is *independent* if
no member of $\Sigma$ is a consequence (modulo the group axioms) of the remaining members.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.64»

/--
A quasiidentity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$(u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v,$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. Whether a group
satisfies such a formula depends only on the classes of these words modulo the group axioms, so
the words are represented as elements of the free group on `Fin n`. The case $k = 0$ (no premises)
gives the identities.
-/
structure Quasiidentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_i = v_i$, as pairs of words $(u_i, v_i)$. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as the pair of words $(u, v)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

namespace Quasiidentity

/--
A group `G` satisfies the quasiidentity `q` if for every assignment `x` of the variables in `G`
under which all the premises of `q` hold, the conclusion of `q` holds. Words are evaluated at `x`
by the homomorphism `FreeGroup.lift x`.
-/
def Holds (q : Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/-- A group `G` satisfies a set `S` of quasiidentities if it satisfies every member of `S`. -/
def SetHolds (S : Set Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, q.Holds G

/--
The quasiidentity `q` is a consequence of the set `S` of quasiidentities (modulo the group
axioms): every group satisfying `S` satisfies `q`.
-/
def Follows (S : Set Quasiidentity) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G → q.Holds G

/--
A set `S` of quasiidentities is independent if no member of `S` is a consequence of the
remaining members of `S`.
-/
def Independent (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Follows (S \ {q}) q

/--
The quasiidentity `q` holds in the class `𝒦` of groups if every group in `𝒦` satisfies `q`.
-/
def HoldsInClass (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G → q.Holds G

/--
A set `S` of quasiidentities is a basis of quasiidentities of the class `𝒦` of groups if a group
satisfies `S` exactly when it satisfies every quasiidentity that holds in the class `𝒦`.
Equivalently, `S` consists of quasiidentities holding in `𝒦` and every quasiidentity holding in
`𝒦` is a consequence of `S`.
-/
def IsBasis (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G ↔ ∀ q, HoldsInClass 𝒦 q → q.Holds G

/-- The commutative law $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$, an identity (a quasiidentity with no premises). -/
def commLaw : Quasiidentity where
  numVars := 2
  premises := []
  conclusion := (.of 0 * .of 1, .of 1 * .of 0)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem commLaw_holds (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : commLaw.Holds G := by
  intro x _
  simp [commLaw, mul_comm]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_commLaw_holds_equiv_perm_fin_three : ¬ commLaw.Holds (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) := by
  intro h
  have := h ![Equiv.swap 0 1, Equiv.swap 1 2] (by simp [commLaw])
  simp [commLaw] at this
  exact absurd (congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe this) 0) (by decide)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem Follows.of_mem {S : Set Quasiidentity} {q : Quasiidentity} (hq : q ∈ S) : Follows S q :=
  fun _ _ hS => hS q hq

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem independent_empty : Independent ∅ := by
  simp [Independent]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBasis.holdsInClass {𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop} {S : Set Quasiidentity}
    (hS : IsBasis 𝒦 S) {q : Quasiidentity} (hq : q ∈ S) : HoldsInClass 𝒦 q :=
  fun G _ hG => (hS G).2 (fun _ hq' => hq' G hG) q hq

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBasis.follows {𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop} {S : Set Quasiidentity}
    (hS : IsBasis 𝒦 S) {q : Quasiidentity} (hq : HoldsInClass 𝒦 q) : Follows S q :=
  fun G _ hG => (hS G).1 hG q hq

end Quasiidentity

open Quasiidentity in
/--
Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

That is, is there a set $\Sigma$ of quasiidentities in the language of groups such that
a group satisfies $\Sigma$ exactly when it satisfies every quasiidentity holding in all finite
groups, and no member of $\Sigma$ is a consequence (modulo the group axioms) of the remaining
members of $\Sigma$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.64» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ S : Set Quasiidentity, IsBasis (fun G _ => Finite G) S ∧ Independent S := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.64»

items: Group words in a quasiidentity are represented as elements of `FreeGroup (Fin n)` rather than as raw syntactic terms. Truth of a quasiidentity in a group depends only on the free-group classes of its words, and basis/independence are semantic notions, so an independent basis exists in one representation iff it exists in the other.
Premises are a `List` of word pairs (order/duplicates are semantically irrelevant); the empty list is allowed, so identities count as quasiidentities, as is standard.
Consequence 'modulo the group axioms' is formalized semantically (`Follows`: every group satisfying S satisfies q), which agrees with syntactic derivability from S ∪ group axioms by completeness.

Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following FormalConjectures/Kourovka/1_40.lean. This is harmless: every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, and quasiidentities are universal sentences, so a failure in a larger universe is witnessed by a finitely generated (hence small) subgroup.

`IsBasis` is stated as `∀ G, G ⊨ S ↔ G ⊨ Q(𝒦)` (Mod(S) = quasivariety generated by 𝒦), matching the decomposition note; the API lemmas `IsBasis.holdsInClass` and `IsBasis.follows` (proved) show it implies Mal'cev's formulation `S ⊆ Q(𝒦) ∧ Q(𝒦) ⊆ Cn(S)`, and the converse is immediate.
A class of groups is represented as a predicate `(G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop`; the class of all finite groups is `fun G _ => Finite G` (includes the trivial group).

Bespoke definitions live in the problem file since they are specific to this problem; a reviewer may prefer moving `Quasiidentity` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
